title: Training a Two-Layer Neural Network on XOR
description: Build a 2-2-1 sigmoid neural network in NumPy, train it on the 4 XOR inputs with manual backpropagation, and plot the learned decision boundary.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import NumPy and Matplotlib, define the 4-row XOR input matrix `X` and target column vector `y` (`[[0], [1], [1], [0]]`), and plot the raw points in `(x1, x2)` space.
Define `sigmoid(z)` and its derivative `s * (1 - s)`, then initialize the 2-to-2 hidden layer parameters `W1, b1` and the 2-to-1 output layer parameters `W2, b2`.

Run gradient descent for the supplied epochs with the configured learning rate. Each epoch computes the forward pass (`z1, a1, z2, a2`), MSE `loss`, backward gradients (`dloss_dW2, dloss_db2, dloss_dW1, dloss_db1`), and weight updates.

Compare the forward pass (lines 47-50) with the backward pass (lines 56-66). `dloss_dz2` multiplies `dloss_da2` by `sigmoid_deriv(z2)`. It then propagates the error back through `W2.T` into the hidden layer (`dloss_da1 = dloss_dz2 @ W2.T`).

steps.question: After training on `y = [[0], [1], [1], [0]]`, which two rows of `X` should have final predictions `a2` near `1.0`? Which two should be near `0.0`?
steps.answer: Inputs `[0, 1]` and `[1, 0]` have predictions near `1.0` (`0.972` and `0.966`), while `[0, 0]` and `[1, 1]` have predictions near `0.0` (`0.030` and `0.027`).

steps.description: Evaluate the trained network on a meshgrid to plot the nonlinear contour boundary. Then run `predict(Xtest)` on the 4 training inputs plus `[0.2, 0.8]` (`0.624`) and `[0.9, 0.9]` (`0.027`).
